kicker: When it reads, an AI lets every word look around the whole sentence — like lighting a lantern toward the words it needs.
summary: An AI understands each word by looking at the whole sentence — and in a long text, it remembers the start and the end best.

quiz.q: You paste a 50-page document into an AI and need it to do one thing right. Where should the request go?
options: In the middle, next to the most relevant part
At the start or at the end of it
Anywhere — the AI reads it all evenly
In capital letters so the AI notices
quiz.explain: In a long text, an AI usually remembers the start and the end better than the middle.

lantern.label: Lanterns on a sentence
lantern.art: Looking down from a wooden bridge: under a small high moon, a river of ink winds in an S from the foot of the bridge to the horizon. Each word of the sentence is a paper lantern drifting with the current, large when near, small when far; the last two words wait unlit in an eddy. Touch the word “it”: its lantern flares, lifts off the water and casts threads of moonlight to every word, the brightest to the word it needs most. Drag the lantern from the eddy to the end of the sentence and the brightest thread swings elsewhere.
lantern.prompt: Touch the word “it” — who is it?
lantern.swapPrompt: Drag the eddy’s lantern onto the word “slow”
lantern.decode: The brighter the thread, the more the AI leans on that word
lantern.pivotAria: Touch the word “it” to see which word it attends to (or press Enter)
lantern.swapAria: Change the last word of the sentence to “{word}”
lantern.threadAria: The word “it” attends most strongly to “{word}”

weightsNote.text: The brightness of the threads is an illustration set by AI Zen, not measured from a real model.

insight.text: Change only the last word and “it” turns from the cat into the mouse: an AI understands a word by looking at the whole sentence.

detail.text: This way of reading is called attention. In 2019, probing the BERT model, researchers found it really does link pronouns to the right person or thing mentioned.

heads.label: Many heads, many gazes
heads.art: A moon pond in a night stone garden. Four stone lanterns stand at its corners, each in its own shade of ink: deep black, pale grey, smoky blue, vermilion. Nine paper rafts on the water carry the nine words of the sentence. Light a lantern: a cone of light falls through the mist onto the pond, and the words that lantern joins arc up as bands of light, each lantern at its own height. From above the bands tangle; bring your eye down to the water and they part into four tiers.
heads.aria: A 3D moon pond with four stone lanterns and nine word rafts
heads.hint: Drag to turn the garden, scroll or pinch to come closer, double-tap or press Home to return. Arrow keys turn it too; keys 1 to 4 light the lanterns.
heads.orbit: Drag down to look along the water
heads.decode: Each lantern = one way the AI looks at the sentence

heads.name: Who did it?
heads.aria: Light lantern 1: links “praised” to who praised, “The teacher”

heads.name: Did what?
heads.aria: Light lantern 2: links “praised” to what was praised, “the essay”

heads.name: The word before
heads.relation: each word looks at the word just before it
heads.aria: Light lantern 3: each word looks at the word just before it

heads.name: What is “it”?
heads.aria: Light lantern 4: links the word “it” to “the essay”

headsNote.text: Real heads usually mix more kinds than the drawing shows.

insight.text: Four lanterns light the same sentence, each catching a different link — the AI reads in several ways at once.

detail.text: Each such “lantern” is called an attention head. The original Transformer (2017) had 8 heads per layer.

layers.label: Layer upon layer
layers.art: A deep pond cut out like a block and floating in the night: water, lily pads and the moon on top; a glass-clear cut face where the water lies in bands like silk, the ink deepening toward the bottom; rock walls with roots; 96 fine marks along the cut edge in three bands. A pebble carved with the word “it” sinks; with each band the word gains another coat of ink, until at the bottom it rests beside a scroll: the essay.
layers.sentence: The teacher praised the essay by Lan because it was superb
layers.sliderAria: Drag the “it” pebble down through the layers (← → keys)

stages.reads: “it” is a thing, not a person

steps: 2 layers to go — keep dragging down
The deepest layer — drag to the bottom

stagesNote.text: The three steps here are an illustration.

insight.text: The more layers it passes, the clearer “it” becomes to the AI: from a pronoun to exactly Lan’s essay.

detail.text: In 2019, probing the BERT model, researchers found the first layers handle grammar, and only later layers link a pronoun to the right thing.

window.label: How far the window reaches
window.art: In a tea room, facing a long wall of paper sliding doors; the moon is a glow behind the paper. Drag the moon through the years and panel after panel slides open onto a deep garden: at each milestone a stele rises carrying what an AI could read in one go: a single letter, a few pages, a novel, and today a stack of about ten; far back in the mist stands a pale bookshelf, the 10-million figure its maker states itself. At today a long scroll unrolls on the mats: drag the vermilion seal “what matters” along it, and the reading lamp burns bright at both ends of the scroll and dims in the middle.
window.prompt: Drag the moon through the years
window.prompt2: Drag the vermilion seal along the scroll
window.decode: The window = how much text an AI can read in one go. 1 million tokens ≈ over 700,000 words.
window.sealAria: The vermilion seal “what matters”: drag it along the scroll from start to end (← → keys)

fact.text: Eight researchers publish the Transformer: the AI reads the whole sentence at once through attention instead of word by word — which later lets it read very long texts.
GPT-3 reads at most 2,048 tokens at a time: a few pages of text.
Anthropic raises how much Claude can read to 100,000 tokens, about 75,000 words: enough for a short novel in one go.

horizon.text: Many leading models now read about 1 million tokens at a time — some 9–10 such novels.

insight.text: An AI can read a whole stack of books, but it remembers the start and the end best — the middle is easily missed.

detail.text: Tip: put what matters at the start or end of a long prompt (Liu et al., 2023).

growth.text: From GPT-3 (2,048 tokens, 2020) to today (about 1 million), the window has grown nearly 500-fold.

vaswani-2017.title: Attention Is All You Need
vaswani-2017.note: The paper introducing the Transformer: attention only, no recurrence or convolution; section 3.2.2 uses h = 8 attention heads, section 3.1 uses N = 6 layers.

clark-2019.title: What Does BERT Look At? An Analysis of BERT's Attention
clark-2019.note: Some attention heads match grammatical relations and coreference (linking a pronoun to what it refers to), e.g. the direct object of a verb.

jain-wallace-2019.title: Attention is not Explanation
jain-wallace-2019.note: Attention weights often disagree with other measures of importance; very different attention distributions can yield the same prediction.

tenney-2019.title: BERT Rediscovers the Classical NLP Pipeline
tenney-2019.note: Parts of speech and syntax are captured in lower regions of the network, then entities, semantic roles and coreference in higher ones.

gpt3-2020.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners (GPT-3)
gpt3-2020.note: Table 2.1: GPT-3 175B has 96 layers and 96 attention heads; all models use a 2,048-token context window.

anthropic-100k.title: Introducing 100K Context Windows
anthropic-100k.note: Claude’s context window grows from 9K to 100K tokens, about 75,000 words.

google-gemini-15.title: Our next-generation model: Gemini 1.5
google-gemini-15.note: Limited preview up to 1 million tokens (1 hour of video, 11 hours of audio, over 700,000 words); Google says it tested up to 10 million tokens in research.

meta-llama4.title: The Llama 4 herd
meta-llama4.note: Meta announces Llama 4 Scout with a 10-million-token context window (the company’s own claim).

anthropic-1m-ga.title: 1M context is now generally available for Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6
anthropic-1m-ga.note: A 1-million-token window becomes generally available for Claude Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6. Pricing and features change often; check the official page.

lost-in-middle.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
lost-in-middle.note: Performance is usually highest when the needed information sits at the start or end of the context, and drops clearly when it sits in the middle.
